newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea's NLCF sees more stable grain prices in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Korea's NLCF sees more stable grain prices in 1997.

text.p: Rising world grain output, in response to the strong prices seen earlier this year, should balance surging demand for feed grain in East Asia and ensure more stable prices in 1997, South Korea's NLCF said on Tuesday.

"We are not expecting a roller coaster of volatile prices next year," Lee Byung Yul, general manager of the Feed & Foreign Trade Department of the National Livestock Co-operatives Federation (NLCF) told Reuters in an interview.

NLCF is the world's second largest buyer of feed grain after Japanese co-operative Zen Noh and will have imported 3.8 million tonnes of feedstuffs worth $660 million this year compared with 3.1 million tonnes worth $420 million in 1995.

Lee said U.S. moves to cutback on supply restriction measures such as the Acreage Reduction Program (ARP) and the increased yield from genetically-altered crop strains, should combine to boost grain production in the United States.
"We don't see any significant supply/demand deficit. Virtually every major producer appears to have an abundant crop so inventories can be carried forward into next year."

Lee said that while feed demand remained strong on the back of rising meat consumption in the rapidly growing East Asian economies, he did not expect this to overwhelm the robust outlook for the supply side in 1997.
"The U.S. winter wheat crop is looking very good and so is the Brazilian soy crop," he said.

The NLCF forecasts South Korea's total feed consumption will continue its rapid growth and peak at around 18 million tonnes a year at the end of the century, compared to current demand of about 16 million tonnes.
Lee said the co-operative expects to increase its share of this market to around 30 percent in 2002 from just over 24 percent in 1995.

He said this expansion in market share would be achieved partly at the expense of the private sector, but also through the replacement of old feed mill equipment to increase installed capacity and to improve production efficiency.
